title: Axial-flux motor
summary: Implemented the transmitter, receiver and Arduino code for the shared motor build, documented in bench footage.
work: Implemented the transmitter, receiver and Arduino code; Tuna created the motor CAD.
Shared the winding and assembly work, combining the handheld potentiometer, paired NRF24L01 modules, motor-side Arduino and ESC.
limits: Hand-wound motor construction, printed mechanics and wireless Arduino/ESC control, accompanied by an interactive explanation of the drive system.
credit: Two-person build with Tuna, who created the motor CAD. Original media: Kubilay Uluçay.

title: Three-axis camera gimbal
summary: Developed most of the Arduino code and shared the build and gyroscope cross-checks; CAD adaptation by Tuna.
work: Wrote most of the Arduino code; Tuna handled CAD adaptation, with the physical build and integration shared.
Compared phone gyroscope readings with onboard sensor data for feedback and cross-checking.
The interactive exhibit explains counter-rotation and the relationship between the three axes.
limits: Servo actuation, gyroscope feedback and mechanical integration; exhibit sliders explore full-turn orientations in the explanatory model.
credit: Two-person build with Tuna, who handled CAD adaptation from a sourced design.

title: Battery management system
summary: Completed most development and all Simulink simulations for the four-cell BMS; PCB drawings by Atahan.
work: Developed the research and system plan in EE401, followed by circuit fabrication, instrumentation and STM32 integration in EE402.
Built the cell-sensing and capacitor-transfer circuitry and modeled active balancing in MATLAB/Simulink.
The interactive model explores cell voltage, load, temperature, balancing and thermal protection.
limits: Four-cell sensing, custom PCB fabrication, STM32 control and capacitor-based balancing, with an illustrative accelerated-time model.
credit: Senior-year team project. Most development and all simulations by Kubilay Uluçay; PCB drawings by Atahan.

title: Boundary-scanning Zumo robot
summary: Developed most of the robot project, combining boundary navigation with IR detection counts and LED/buzzer reporting.
work: Calibrate reflectance sensors, move toward the white edge while avoiding IR detections, then scan and return.
Record counts across repeated scans and signal the largest observed count through the LED and buzzer.
Integrated reflectance calibration, IR detection, motor control and boundary-response logic.
limits: Boundary navigation and IR detection counting, documented through the team firmware and report and explained in an interactive arena.
credit: Yunus Emre Ozan and Seyit Kubilay Uluçay. Uses Pololu Zumo libraries.

title: Power flow & economic dispatch
summary: An individual MATLAB app using demand balance and equal marginal costs for three-generator dispatch.
work: Two modes expose power flow and economic dispatch with three generators.
The dispatch callback solves equal marginal-cost equations with a demand constraint, then calculates quadratic costs.
The source includes fixed network coefficients and UI controls for generator settings.
limits: An academic four-bus network and three-generator cost model implemented in MATLAB App Designer.
credit: Named individual MATLAB submission by Kubilay Uluçay.

title: Off-grid residential PV design
summary: Autonomy-led PVsyst sizing, but roughly 62-year simple payback at May 2025 prices: independence rather than bill savings.
work: Sized an eight-module 580 W array (4.64 kW) and a 48 V storage system for a residential off-grid design.
Weather, load, storage and winter availability drive the simulation trade-offs.
Compared capital costs, household energy demand and grid billing using the study's May 2025 assumptions.
limits: A 2025 PVsyst design study covering array sizing, storage autonomy, annual energy balance and financial feasibility.
credit: Seyit Kubilay Uluçay and Mehmet Fatih Karaosman.

title: Wind-farm interconnection trade-offs
summary: Compared 27 configurations and recommended Experiment 9: CONDOR connections to PETE and PAI.
work: PowerWorld cases compare cost, loss and overload constraints for a hypothetical 200 MW wind-farm connection.
Compared feasible configurations across construction cost, network loading and electrical losses.
limits: An EE101 PowerWorld network study comparing conductor and substation configurations for wind generation.

title: PLC sequences: traffic lights & toy claw
summary: Developed sequence logic and checked simulated traffic-light modes and claw-game control.
work: Traffic-light logic models normal and after-hours modes with HMI controls.
The claw game uses a coin input, a 90-second positioning window and a staged gripper sequence.
Documented state diagrams, HMI screens, timers and simulation observations for both control scenarios.
limits: Team coursework in PLC sequencing and operator interfaces, developed in Control Expert simulation.
credit: Berke Çeçen, Efe Can Özhan, Genco Güven and Kubilay Uluçay.

title: Bench measurements & diode curves
summary: Selected bench records show multimeter readings, resistor-current calculations and diode I–V observations.
work: Built the lab circuits and recorded node and resistor voltage measurements.
Compared the recorded current–voltage behavior of different diode types.
limits: Selected original bench pages, not a complete lab series or new measurements.
credit: Original EE301 bench records by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, Fall 2023.

title: Sensors, timing & motor response
summary: Four selected studies connect analog sensing, timing waveforms, two-board I2C and proportional motor response.
work: Recorded analog-input and reflectance-sensor behavior and an oscillator timing capture.
Adapted course examples for a button-to-LED I2C link between two Arduino boards.
Documented motor-position observations at different proportional gains; the later full-PID extension was not verified.
limits: Selected original source pages with original page references, not a complete lab series or a validated full-PID controller.
credit: Original ME417 records by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, March–May 2024; course examples retain their authorship.

title: Engineering verification at Accenture
summary: Requirements-based verification for clinical-laboratory automation: Python/Gherkin tests, failure investigation and requirement-to-test traceability.
work: Develop requirements-based black-box tests and refactor test functions and state-change checks through reviewed GitLab merge requests.
Run existing local and GitLab/AWS test pipelines, investigate test and suspected product issues, and maintain traceability in Codebeamer.
limits: A public account of engineering verification work; client-specific requirements, source code and internal results remain confidential.
credit: Quality Assurance Engineer, Accenture Industry X, January 2026–present.

title: Floor sensing in an R&D team
summary: Built a motorized sensing rig, processed measurement data in Python/Excel and carried regression models through embedded integration and floor-type project trials.
work: Built a motorized test rig and adapted acquisition code for sensing measurements across environments and configurations.
Preprocessed approximately 650,000 logged data points in Python/Excel using filtering and summary statistics.
Developed regression models in Minitab and integrated the model into embedded firmware.
Evaluated floor-type prediction in project trials with 83.5% prediction success and documented test and integration findings.
limits: A public overview of sensing, data-analysis and embedded-integration contributions within Beko's Advanced Sensor Technologies R&D team.
credit: R&D internship contribution by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay within Beko Advanced Sensor Technologies, July–August 2024.
